summary: On a flash, the camera pulls back from a darkness that reveals itself to be the black eye of a fetus suspended in a placenta-like husk, its malleable skull already growing around a brain-jack. As Morpheus narrates, we learn the Machines discovered a new form of fusion needing only a small electrical charge to initiate, and that the human body generates more bioelectricity than a 120-volt battery plus over 25,000 B.T.U.'s of body heat. The husk hanging from a stalk is plucked by a thresher-like farm machine. Morpheus declares that there are endless fields where human beings are no longer born but grown. We rise up, the field stretching to the horizon, lightning tearing open the sky as a harvester sweeps past.

what_changes.before: Speaking of the Matrix's power source in general terms, having explained that the Machines needed a fusion reaction.
what_changes.after: Revealing the specific horror: that humans are farmed, grown in fields rather than born, as the true source of Machine power.
what_changes.evidence: There are fields, endless fields where human beings are no longer born; we are grown.

what_changes.before: A suspended organism growing in a placenta-like husk, its skull forming around the brain-jack.
what_changes.after: Plucked from its stalk by a thresher-like farm machine, becoming a harvested crop.
what_changes.evidence: The husk hanging from a stalk is plucked by a thresher-like farm machine.

event_hint.one_line: Morpheus reveals the true nature of the Matrix's power source: human beings grown and harvested in endless fields.

_mind_pass: ran: 1 speaker, 133w >= p75 (125w) for this work

minds.wants: To make Neo — and by extension the audience — accept the full, unbearable truth of what humanity has become, pushing the explanation past abstraction into visceral horror.
minds.feels: A grim, almost reverent resolve; he is delivering a truth he has carried for years, one that sickens him, yet he holds his voice steady because the lesson must land. There is a kind of sorrow underneath the lecture — he is showing Neo the corpse of the human race.
minds.shows: A calm, measured, documentary narrator's voice. He lets nothing of his revulsion leak into the tone; the horror is carried entirely by the images he chooses to describe, not by his affect.
minds.basis: The narration is clinical and factual — bioelectricity, BTUs, fusion — even as the images escalate to 'human beings are no longer born; we are grown' and the harvester sweeping the field. The steadiness of the delivery against the atrocity of the content is the gap. sc-040 established his pedagogical method: he lets the visual and verbal reveal do the emotional work while he remains composed ('The desert of the real').

believes_about.belief: That Neo can withstand being shown the truth directly, that the shock of it is a necessary and survivable part of waking him.
believes_about.wrong_because: The event shape shows Neo's mind physically rejects the influx — he will thrash, scream, and require restraint before collapsing unconscious. Morpheus has misjudged, or has chosen to override, how much Neo can take, and this miscalculation costs Neo a violent ordeal. (His apology in ev-010 for 'breaking the rule against freeing older minds' suggests he knows he pushed too hard.)

connects_back: sc-039: the brain-jack and coaxial 'cerebrum chip' planted in Neo's neck is the same interface the fetus is shown growing into, linking Neo's own body to the farmed bodies.

sc-040: Morpheus's Construct-based method of teaching through descending revelation ('the desert of the real') continues here; the fetus fields are the logical, physical proof of the ruined world he just showed Neo.
sc-040: the earlier mention that 'we have only bits and pieces of information' about history frames this as the moment Morpheus delivers what they know for certain about the power source.
sets_up: ev-010: Neo's physical and mental rejection of this revelation leads directly to his collapse and unconscious state, and to Morpheus's later apology for having pushed too hard.
ev-010: the horror of being 'grown' as a power source raises the stakes of the prophecy Morpheus is about to introduce — the value and fragility of a freed human mind.
The film's central horror is now established as fact, so that everything that follows — training, the rescue, Neo's growing power — is understood against the reality that humans are livestock.
dramatic_function: This is the revelation of the film's true horror — the moment the abstract idea of the Matrix as a prison becomes the concrete image of humanity as a farmed crop. It converts Neo's (and the viewer's) philosophical unease into visceral dread and completes the 'desert of the real' lesson by showing what the Machines do with the bodies trapped inside it.
